jobs.description:
Work Location:

Toronto, Ontario, Canada

Hours

Line Of Business

Risk Management

Pay Details

$185,000 - $275,000 CAD

TD is committed to providing fair and equitable compensation opportunities to all colleagues. Growth opportunities and skill development are defining features of the colleague experience at TD. Our compensation policies and practices have been designed to allow colleagues to progress through the salary range over time as they progress in their role. The base pay actually offered may vary based upon the candidate's skills and experience, job-related knowledge, geographic location, and other specific business and organizational needs.

As a candidate, you are encouraged to ask compensation related questions and have an open dialogue with your recruiter who can provide you more specific details for this role.

Job Description

We are looking for a strategic and collaborative executive to shape and deliver the enterprise Risk Data Strategy. As Vice President, Risk Data Strategy and Transformation, you will lead the roadmap, governance, quality, architecture, and lifecycle management of Risk data products and platforms, building capabilities that strengthen risk management, regulatory compliance, analytics, reporting, and decision-making.

Reporting to the Senior Vice President, Risk Transformation and Enablement, you will work across Risk Management and with enterprise partners to modernize data capabilities, strengthen governance, and enable scalable, transparent, and resilient solutions. This is an opportunity to influence enterprise priorities and advance data-informed decision-making in a highly regulated environment.

Key Accountabilities

Set the enterprise Risk Data Strategy, target-state capabilities, investment priorities, and multi-year roadmap.
Lead the governance and lifecycle management of Risk data products and platforms, including ownership, quality, lineage, standards, and controls.
Shape the evolution of Risk data architecture and integration strategies to support scalable, transparent, and resilient capabilities.
Translate Risk priorities into practical roadmaps, including the technology, data, governance, and implementation considerations required for delivery.
Lead portfolio planning and prioritization for Risk data initiatives, balancing strategic value, capacity, dependencies, regulatory expectations, and risk.
Oversee the funding, delivery, benefits tracking, and value realization of Risk data products and initiatives.
Establish governance and reporting that give senior leaders clear visibility into progress, outcomes, risks, issues, and decisions.
Advance data modernization by applying emerging technologies, industry trends, and leading practices where they add value.
Anticipate and manage delivery risks, resolve obstacles, and bring forward timely recommendations and trade-offs.
Build strong partnerships across Risk, Technology, Enterprise Data and Analytics, Finance, Regulatory Reporting, and other shared-service teams.
Lead with empathy and transparency, creating an environment where colleagues feel heard, supported, and confident navigating change.
Develop an inclusive, high-performing environment where different perspectives are valued and teams are empowered to deliver.

Key Partnerships

Risk Management leaders and teams across all Risk pillars.
Enterprise partners across Risk Technology, Enterprise Data and Analytics, Enterprise Architecture, Finance, Regulatory Reporting, Governance and Control, and shared services.
Senior executives, governance forums, and program sponsors responsible for strategic prioritization and decision-making.
Product, platform, architecture, and delivery teams responsible for building and sustaining Risk data capabilities.

What You Bring

Significant leadership experience in one or more of the following areas: data strategy, data management, data products, technology, analytics, transformation, or risk management.
Experience leading complex, enterprise-scale data initiatives and operating model change in a matrixed organization.
A track record of translating strategy into clear priorities, practical roadmaps, and measurable outcomes.
Strong judgment and the ability to influence, challenge constructively, and build alignment with senior leaders and cross-functional partners.
Experience with data governance, data quality, architecture, data products, platform operating models, portfolio planning, or benefits tracking.
Experience with data technology and product management across major platforms and tools. Familiarity with Rahona, Technology Asset Platform, Databricks, Power BI, or comparable technologies is an asset.
Ability to navigate ambiguity, competing priorities, and regulatory or operational pressure while maintaining momentum.
Inclusive leadership skills and a commitment to creating an environment where people with different backgrounds and perspectives can contribute and succeed.
Demonstrated emotional intelligence and executive presence, with the ability to listen with curiosity, build trust, navigate sensitive conversations, and bring diverse stakeholders together through complex change.
A post-secondary degree or an equivalent combination of relevant education and experience. Advanced education or professional credentials may be an asset but are not required.

We recognize that strong candidates may bring different combinations of education, career paths, and lived experience. We encourage you to apply even if you do not meet every qualification listed.

Who We Are

TD is one of the world's leading global financial institutions and is the fifth largest bank in North America by branches/stores. Every day, we strive to make every interaction, product, and experience remarkably human and refreshingly simple for over 27 million households and businesses in Canada, the United States and around the world. More than 95,000 TD colleagues bring their skills, talent, and creativity to foster deeper relationships, ensure disciplined execution, and build a simpler, faster banking experience. TD is deeply committed to being a leader in client experience, that is why we believe that all colleagues, no matter where they work, are client facing. Together, we are reimagining what banking can be for our clients, colleagues and communities.

Our Total Rewards Package

Our Total Rewards package reflects the investments we make in our colleagues to help them and their families achieve their financial, physical, and mental well-being goals. Total Rewards at TD includes a base salary, variable compensation, and several other key plans such as health and well-being benefits, savings and retirement programs, paid time off, banking benefits and discounts, career development, and reward and recognition programs. Learn more

Additional Information

We’re delighted that you’re considering building a career with TD. Through regular development conversations, training programs, and a competitive benefits plan, we’re committed to providing the support our colleagues need to thrive both at work and at home.

Please be advised that this job opportunity is subject to provincial regulation for employment purposes. It is imperative to acknowledge that each province or territory within the jurisdiction of Canada may have its own set of regulations, requirements.

Colleague Development

If you’re interested in a specific career path or are looking to build certain skills, we want to help you succeed. You’ll have regular career, development, and performance conversations with your manager, as well as access to an online learning platform and a variety of mentoring programs to help you unlock future opportunities.

If you’re passionate about helping clients and building deep, lasting relationships, TD offers diverse career paths where you can grow your expertise and make a meaningful impact.

We're committed to your success and foster a respectful workplace where diverse perspectives are valued, everyone has fair opportunities to grow, and you can unlock your full potential to achieve your career goals. Here at TD, we hire and develop the best.

Training & Onboarding

We will provide training and onboarding sessions to ensure that you’ve got everything you need to succeed in your new role.

Interview Process

We’ll reach out to candidates of interest to schedule an interview. We do our best to communicate outcomes to all applicants by email or phone call.

Accommodation

Your accessibility is important to us. Please let us know if you’d like accommodations (including accessible meeting rooms, captioning for virtual interviews, etc.) to help us remove barriers so that you can participate throughout the interview process.

We look forward to hearing from you!

jobs.description:
Permanent Full Time

As the Director, Enterprise Data Enablement, you will be responsible for enabling cross-business insights and will own the Canada Operations and Business Enablement’s (COBE) alignment to the Enterprise Data Strategy.

The Director will operate as an enabler, and will partner with our Business Leaders to identify and prioritize cross-business unit data use cases that will deliver measurable value for the organization. Success in this role will be measured by value realization through these insights, which will be achieved through influence, strong stakeholder relationships, and a deep understanding of both business outcomes and data capabilities.

In addition, this role ensures enterprise data standards, governance, and policies are adopted consistently, connects COBE data owners and sources with enterprise data platforms, and represents COBE priorities across enterprise data forums.

What You Will Do

Work with business leaders to understand, identify and prioritize cross-business unit data insights and potential business benefits.
Partner with Technology to understand the One Canada Life view of data and would work closely with the Business stakeholders to identify insights that would enable the biggest impact.
Guide business teams on the responsible use of customer data to enable data‑driven business insights and decision‑making, while balancing innovation with ethical, legal, and regulatory requirements, and providing leadership oversight.
Act as a connector across business, technology, and enablement teams to identify data risks early, surface issues, and enable informed decision-making.
Establish strong enterprise data governance across classification, retention, and access, and lead the implementation and ongoing management of the Enterprise Data Governance tool.
Enable and facilitate the utilization of enterprise data governance practices across Canada Operations & Business Enablement, ensuring alignment with corporate policies, regulatory expectations, and risk appetite.
Enable scalable, reusable and insightful data assets by aligning COBE needs with enterprise data capabilities.
Contribute to data literacy and awareness by enabling education, forums, and guidance that translate data into informed, timely, and impactful business decisions across leaders and teams.

10+ years of experience in data management, data governance, data enablement, or enterprise data roles.
Strong ability to bridge business needs and technology, with ability to provide data insights that will enable decision-making
Exceptional stakeholder leadership and partnership skills, with confidence engaging senior business, technology, risk, and compliance leaders
Excellent communication and problem-solving skills
Senior leadership experience at the Director level within data governance, data enablement, risk, or related functions in complex, highly regulated environments.
Deep knowledge of data governance, risk, and control frameworks, including data quality, metadata management, access controls, retention, and privacy.
Hands-on experience with enterprise data strategies and operating models, including implementing and running data governance tooling such as data catalogs, lineage, metadata, or stewardship platforms.
Strong systems-thinking capability, balancing data protection and risk management with enabling analytics, AI, and insight-driven decision-making.
Comfort operating in highly matrixed organizations, using influence, education, prioritization, and relationship-building to define value, manage stakeholders, and drive outcomes

Typically 7+ years of relevant experience and a post-secondary degree in a related field of study or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Completion of relevant investment certifications or designations (e.g., CIM, CFA, MBA, or comparable industry credential).
Experience owning investment products, managed account programs, advisory platforms, investment platforms, or portfolio solutions.
Proven ability to define product strategy, develop business cases, and execute strategic roadmaps.
Strong understanding of managed accounts, SMA programs, investment products, advisory platforms, fee-based wealth programs, and unified wealth platforms.
Experience leading complex business, operational, and technology transformation initiatives.
Experience balancing advisor, client, operational, regulatory, and business requirements when designing solutions and implementing change.
Knowledge of pricing and fee architecture, including pricing frameworks, fee administration processes, fee calculation methodologies, advisor compensation models, and revenue modelling.
Experience with wealth technology platforms and translating business requirements into scalable platform capabilities and solutions.
Knowledge of Canadian wealth management regulatory requirements, governance frameworks, risk management practices, and policy development.
Strong analytical, financial modelling, problem-solving, and data-driven decision-making skills.
Exceptional communication, stakeholder management, influencing, and relationship-building skills, with the ability to align priorities and obtain buy-in across diverse stakeholder groups.
Demonstrated ability to manage ambiguity, exercise sound judgment, and navigate complex business challenges.
Knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite, including Excel, PowerPoint, Power BI, Copilot, and emerging AI-enabled productivity tools.

jobs.title: Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, Trilogy (Remote) - $800,000/year USD
jobs.description:
Most finance executives inherit a system. You will redesign one, then decide where the capital goes.

Trilogy is looking for the executive who can turn a portfolio of businesses into a capital allocation system: continuously ranking where the next dollar should go, backing those decisions with rigorous models, and moving capital toward its highest-return uses. You will own the calls that matter: fund or kill a business line; invest or hold; acquire or walk away; refinance or pay down debt. Every recommendation must connect strategy to cash, liquidity, covenants, risk, and enterprise value.

Just as important, you will architect an AI-native finance function built to scale without decision bottlenecks. This does not mean sprinkling AI tools onto a traditional finance organization. You will redesign reporting, planning, controls, portfolio monitoring, and decision support around what AI and automation can now do. You won't need to personally build every workflow, but you must use AI deeply enough to know its edges: where it accelerates analysis, where it fails, and where expert judgment must take over. The result should be a smaller, more senior, higher-leverage finance organization rather than a growing pyramid of people and processes.

You will operate directly with Trilogy's CEO, board, lenders, and capital partners, with personal accountability for the financial truth behind major decisions. This is an $800K W-2 salaried role for someone who has already earned credibility at serious financial scale and now wants the mandate to compound enterprise value across an entire portfolio. If you want your impact measured by the quality of your capital decisions and the financial system you leave behind, apply.

What You Will Be Doing

Allocating capital across the portfolio: Run capital and portfolio reviews, rank competing uses of capital on risk-adjusted return, and make clear fund, hold, restructure, exit, debt-paydown, or acquisition recommendations.
Architecting an AI-native finance system: Redesign planning, reporting, consolidation, controls, portfolio monitoring, and financial workflows around AI, automation, and scalable systems rather than additional headcount.
Driving investments and transactions: Build and defend the financial case for strategic investments, M&A, financing, and refinancing, including integrated models, downside scenarios, capital structure, covenant implications, and execution plans.
Owning board and capital-partner communication: Give the CEO, board, lenders, and capital partners fast, quantified, defensible truth, with recommendations that make the decision and trade-offs explicit.
Building a high-leverage finance leadership team: Set the bar for a small group of exceptional finance leaders while creating systems that allow new ventures and greater complexity to be absorbed without linear organizational growth.

What You Won’t Be Doing

Running finance as a reporting factory. Closing the books and producing audit workpapers are the Controller's responsibilities. Your job is to turn financial information into better capital decisions.
Building a large finance organization to handle complexity. Scale should come from better systems, AI leverage, automation, and exceptional people, not layers of management.
Adding AI as a superficial productivity tool. You will architect workflows around its real capabilities and limitations, which requires substantial firsthand use.
Producing strategy decks without financial consequences. Major recommendations must carry the integrated model, downside case, capital implications, and execution guardrails behind them.
Managing the board through narrative. The numbers, assumptions, risks, and recommended action should be clear enough to withstand scrutiny.

Executive Vice President And Chief Financial Officer Key Responsibilities

Build a durable, AI-native finance function that compounds enterprise value across Trilogy's portfolio by allocating capital to its highest-return uses and creating financial systems and controls that scale without decision bottlenecks.

Basic Requirements

Experience as the most senior finance decision-maker, or their direct deputy, for a business or portfolio with $100M+ in annual revenue across multiple legal entities.
Personal ownership of major capital-allocation decisions, including the ability to explain what was funded, reduced, or rejected; the dollars involved; the trade-offs; and your recommendation.
Decision ownership on at least one $25M+ closed M&A, financing, or refinancing transaction, with direct responsibility for negotiation, financing selection, board recommendation, or post-close integration.
Direct experience presenting to and taking live questions from a board of directors.
Ownership of an external audit relationship under US GAAP or IFRS, directly or through a Controller reporting to you.
Hands-on experience with a true enterprise ERP such as SAP, NetSuite, Oracle, Workday, or equivalent.
Recent experience re-architecting a finance workflow around AI, with enough regular personal AI use to understand where the technology is reliable, where it is not, and how those boundaries should shape finance-system design.
Ability to operate integrated 3-statement models and defend assumptions, downside scenarios, covenant math, capital structure, and recommendations under live questioning.
Strong written and verbal English, with experience communicating directly with CEOs, boards, lenders, or capital partners.
Located within the UTC−8 to UTC+3 time-zone range.

Nice-to-have Requirements

CPA, ACA, ACCA, CIMA, CFA, MBA, or comparable finance credential.
Earlier career experience in private equity, investment banking, M&A, corporate finance, or another environment requiring rigorous modeling and high-stakes capital decisions.
Experience rebuilding a finance function rather than simply inheriting and operating one.
Experience across a portfolio, multi-entity, or PE-backed operating environment.

About Trilogy

Hundreds of software businesses run on the Trilogy Business Platform. For three decades, Trilogy has been known for 3 things: Relentlessly seeking top talent, innovating new technology, and incubating new businesses.

Our technological innovation is spearheaded by a passion for simple customer-facing designs. Our incubation of new businesses ranges from entirely new moon-shot ideas to rearchitecting existing projects for today's modern cloud-based stack.

Trilogy is a place where you can be surrounded with great people, be proud of doing great work, and grow your career in leaps and bounds.

There is so much to cover for this exciting role, and space here is limited. Hit the Apply button if you found this interesting and want to learn more. We look forward to meeting you!

Working with us

This is a full-time (40 hours per week), long-term position. The position is immediately available and requires entering into an independent contractor agreement with Crossover as a Contractor of Record. The compensation level for this role is $400 USD/hour, which equates to $800,000 USD/year assuming 40 hours per week and 50 weeks per year. The payment period is weekly. jobs.description:
Founded in 2000 by three former Royal Canadian Air Force (RCAF) CF-18 fighter pilots who identified an opportunity to improve military readiness training, Top Aces has since established itself as the world leader in contracted adversary air (ADAIR) services and joint terminal attack controller (JTAC) training.

We pride ourselves on our unblemished safety record, having flown an industry leading 130,000+ hours of operational training without accident in support of customers worldwide, including Canada, the U.S., Germany, and multiple other NATO allies and international partner nations.

Our vision is to be the most trusted provider of innovative defense training solutions, continuously elevating standards in an industry where "Experience Matters." This commitment to innovation and technology ensures we remain adaptable, training allied militaries to succeed against evolving threats.

Top Aces’ dynamic team contributes to delivering on our purpose of training the next generation of combat leaders by living our values of Service, Integrity, Excellence, and Together every day!

Join our team!

Position Summary

The Director of Data Management and Business Intelligence leads the enterprise data function for Top Aces. Reporting to the Chief Information Officer, the Director defines how data is governed, integrated, protected, and used across aviation operations, maintenance and engineering, supply chain, finance, safety, quality, human resources, commercial programs, and executive management.

The role will establish trusted enterprise data products and decision-ready analytics while respecting aviation record integrity, contractual obligations, export controls, data residency, and need-to-know access. A central priority is to improve the quality and usability of data from Ramco and connected systems so that leaders and front-line teams can manage aircraft availability, maintenance execution, material readiness, program performance, and financial results with greater confidence.

Top Aces Business Context

Top Aces provides advanced operational training and aircraft sustainment services to Canada, the United States, NATO members, and allied nations. The company operates globally in a safety-critical and security-sensitive environment that combines flight operations, maintenance and repair, engineering, supply chain, training, and proprietary technology. The data environment therefore requires strong governance across business units, legal entities, jurisdictions, and security domains.

The Director will translate these operating realities into an enterprise data strategy that supports growth, operational readiness, regulatory compliance, and disciplined investment. The role must balance standardization with the access boundaries required for Canadian, U.S., and international programs.

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise Data Strategy and Operating Model

Partner with the CIO to develop and execute a multi-year enterprise data and BI strategy aligned with Top Aces' business strategy, operating model, technology roadmap, and investment priorities.
Create a practical data operating model that defines decision rights, ownership, stewardship, architecture standards, delivery methods, and support responsibilities across corporate and regional teams.
Chair or support the enterprise data governance council and maintain a prioritized roadmap based on operational value, regulatory risk, data quality, and delivery capacity.
Partner with the CIO and U.S. IT and security leadership to establish appropriate data segregation, access controls, and technology control plans for FOCI-related and export-controlled environments, where applicable.

Data Governance Quality and Protection

Establish enterprise policies and standards for data ownership, classification, quality, lineage, retention, archival, residency, access, and acceptable use.
Define authoritative sources and common business terms for critical domains, including aircraft, fleets, components, serialized parts, maintenance programs, work orders, defects, inventory, suppliers, customers, contracts, personnel, and financial dimensions.
Implement data quality controls, issue-management workflows, and scorecards that identify root causes and assign corrective action to accountable data owners.
Work with Cybersecurity, Legal, Export Compliance, Privacy, Quality, and program security personnel to protect personal, proprietary, controlled, and customer information throughout its lifecycle.
Ensure analytics and data-sharing practices comply with applicable contractual clauses, the Canadian Controlled Goods Program, ITAR and EAR requirements, privacy laws, and customer security obligations.

Data Architecture Integration and Platforms

Define the target enterprise data architecture, including ingestion, integration, master and reference data, lakehouse or warehouse services, semantic models, reporting, metadata, and monitoring.
Establish integration patterns and data contracts for Ramco and other enterprise platforms using secure APIs, event-based interfaces, ETL or ELT pipelines, and controlled file exchange where required.
Reduce duplicate datasets and spreadsheet-dependent reporting by creating reusable, governed data products and certified semantic models.
Set engineering standards for observability, reconciliation, change control, testing, performance, resilience, backup, and recovery across the data platform.
Manage the data-platform lifecycle, capacity, licensing, vendor performance, and total cost of ownership, with particular attention to Microsoft Fabric, Azure data services, Power BI, and connected technologies.

Aviation and MRO Data

Lead data remediation and governance for Ramco MRO and ERP, focusing on master data, transactional integrity, usability, reporting structures, and interfaces with finance, supply chain, engineering, and flight operations.
Partner with Maintenance, Engineering, Airworthiness, Quality, Supply Chain, and Operations to improve the completeness and consistency of aircraft configuration, component history, flight hours and cycles, maintenance plans, work packages, defects, technical records, and inventory data.
Preserve the integrity and auditability of approved maintenance and airworthiness records while enabling controlled downstream analytics.
Develop trusted measures for aircraft availability, dispatch reliability, mission-capable status, maintenance schedule compliance, turnaround time, component reliability, inventory availability, and aircraft-on-ground events.
Support data readiness for operational and regulatory audits, customer reporting, contract performance reviews, and fleet-planning decisions.

Business Intelligence and Performance Management

Lead the design and delivery of executive, operational, and functional dashboards using consistent definitions, clear ownership, and traceable data sources.
Build an enterprise performance framework that connects mission delivery, safety, fleet readiness, maintenance, supply chain, program, customer, workforce, and financial measures.
Develop governed self-service analytics so business users can answer routine questions without creating uncontrolled copies of sensitive data.
Improve forecasting and scenario analysis for fleet utilization, maintenance demand, materials, labour capacity, contract delivery, revenue, cash flow, and program profitability.
Maintain a transparent intake and prioritization process for BI requests, balancing regulatory deadlines, operational urgency, enterprise reuse, and expected value.

Advanced Analytics and Artificial Intelligence

Identify and govern analytics and AI use cases such as predictive maintenance, component reliability, inventory optimization, demand forecasting, anomaly detection, and program risk monitoring.
Require documented business ownership, suitable data quality, human oversight, security review, and measurable benefits before analytics or AI solutions move into production.
Coordinate with engineering, operations, and technology teams when operational, training, mission-system, or live and synthetic data may be used, ensuring the work remains within approved classification and authorization boundaries.
Monitor model performance, data drift, access, and business outcomes, and retire solutions that no longer meet operational, security, or financial requirements.

Leadership and Stakeholder Partnership

Build and lead a capable team spanning data governance, architecture, engineering, BI, and analytics; define roles, develop talent, and manage succession for critical skills.
Partner with executives and functional leaders to convert business questions into governed data products, clear measures, and practical decisions.
Create an active network of business data owners and stewards and hold regular reviews of quality, adoption, access, and value realization.
Manage external partners and vendors through clear outcomes, architecture standards, service levels, security requirements, and commercial accountability.
Communicate data risks, progress, tradeoffs, and investment needs to senior leadership in concise business terms.

Education And Experience

Bachelor's degree in computer science, information systems, data engineering, analytics, business, engineering, or a related discipline. A graduate degree or relevant professional certification is an asset.
At least 10 years of progressive experience in data management, analytics, BI, enterprise applications, or data architecture, including at least five years leading teams or major cross-functional programs.
Experience in aerospace, defense, aviation, MRO, or another highly regulated and asset-intensive industry is strongly preferred.
Demonstrated experience improving data quality and reporting in a complex ERP or MRO environment. Direct experience with Ramco is a significant asset; experience with comparable aviation or enterprise platforms is also relevant.
Experience operating across multiple countries, legal entities, or security domains, including Canada and the United States, is preferred.

Technical and Regulatory Knowledge

Strong knowledge of enterprise data architecture, dimensional and semantic modelling, master data management, metadata, data quality, lineage, SQL, APIs, and ETL or ELT integration.
Hands-on understanding of modern cloud data platforms and BI technologies. Experience with Microsoft Fabric, Azure, Power BI, and Microsoft data services is preferred.
Working knowledge of aviation maintenance and supply-chain data, including serialized components, configuration, maintenance planning, technical records, reliability, and inventory transactions.
Familiarity with aviation regulatory and quality environments such as Transport Canada, FAA, EASA, safety management systems, and AS9100 is an asset.
Working knowledge of information classification, access control, auditability, privacy, data residency, the Canadian Controlled Goods Program, ITAR and EAR, CUI safeguards, CMMC, and NIST SP 800-171, as applicable to the role and programs supported.
Ability to obtain and maintain the security clearances, controlled-goods eligibility, and customer or program authorizations required for the position.

Leadership Competencies

Business judgment that connects data investment to safety, mission readiness, contract delivery, customer commitments, and financial performance.
Ability to influence executives, operational leaders, technical specialists, and front-line users without relying solely on formal authority.
Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain data limitations, security constraints, and architectural decisions to non-technical audiences.
Disciplined program leadership, with practical experience managing priorities, budgets, vendors, risks, and organizational change.
Commitment to Top Aces' values of Service, Integrity, Excellence, and Together.
Professional fluency in English is required. French and additional languages us

Jobber exists to help people in small businesses be successful. We work with small home service businesses, like your local plumbers, painters, and landscapers, to transform the way service is delivered through technology. With Jobber, they can quote, schedule, invoice, and collect payments from their customers while providing an easy and professional customer experience. Running a small business today isn’t like it used to be—the way we consume and deliver service is changing rapidly, technology is evolving, and customers expect more. That’s why we put the power and flexibility in their hands to run their businesses how, where, and when they want!

THE PROBLEM YOU’D OWN

Jobber has AI in production, but not yet at its full potential.

We already have AI answering calls, drafting responses, and powering parts of our product. But today, those systems are still fragmented. Some teams are ahead. Others aren’t. Some workflows are intelligent. Others are still manual. And most importantly, the system doesn’t yet think across the product.

A service pro still has to:

Manually follow up on jobs
Piece together context across workflows
Decide what to do next

The platform doesn’t proactively help them run their business. That’s the gap.

The opportunity is to evolve Jobber from: AI-powered features → AI-powered workflows → AI-powered business operations

This role owns that shift. Not a team. Not a feature. The system.

THE CUSTOMER

You’re building for people who don’t have time to think about software.

A plumber finishing their last job at 6 pm
A cleaner managing 30 clients and 5 employees
A landscaper juggling scheduling, payments, and follow-ups

They’re not asking for “AI.” They’re asking:

“What should I do next?”
“Why didn’t this job convert?”
“Who should I follow up with today?”

And eventually:

They shouldn’t have to ask at all.

The Director who succeeds here will understand:

This isn’t about building clever systems; it’s about building systems that remove thinking from already overwhelmed people.

What You’d Own

End-to-end ownership of Jobber’s AI system layer. You’re not owning a single team. You’re owning how intelligence flows across the entire product.

Product + Platform Scope

AI Foundations (models, orchestration, evals, guardrails)
Copilot (user-facing intelligence layer)
Automations (workflow execution layer)
Platform Experience / Marketplace (integration + ecosystem surface)
Emerging surfaces (voice, messaging, cross-product intelligence)

What This Actually Means

You are responsible for:

How decisions get made inside the system
How context moves across workflows
How actions get triggered (and when they shouldn’t)
How we evaluate whether AI is actually working

This includes:

Agentic workflows (reason → decide → act → evaluate)
Cross-product context (jobs, customers, payments, communication)
Reliability, safety, and failure modes
Developer experience for building on top of AI systems

Team Structure

~30 engineers across 4–6 teams
4–6 EMs / Sr EMs reporting into you
Close partnership with Product, Design, Data

What “good” Looks Like

Not “we shipped AI features.”

Instead:

The system proactively recommends and takes actions
Teams build on shared AI primitives, not reinventing them
AI output is reliable, measurable, and improving over time
Engineers trust the system, and move faster because of it
Customers feel like the product is working for them, not just responding

We are not looking for:

Someone who rolled out Copilot internally
Someone who used LLM APIs for features
Someone adjacent to AI

We are looking for someone who has:

Built real systems where AI makes decisions and takes actions in production.

That means experience with:

Agent orchestration (not just prompts)
Tool use and workflow execution
Evaluation (offline + online)
Observability and failure handling
Guardrails and safety in real systems
Tradeoffs between autonomy vs. control

Define how AI should work across Jobber, not just within a team
Build and evolve a multi-team org to execute on that vision
Make tradeoffs between speed, quality, and safety
Push teams beyond feature thinking into system thinking
Challenge assumptions, including leadership’s
Drive adoption across engineering, product, and the company

Leadership

You’ve led orgs through complexity, not just growth.

Managed managers across multiple teams
Built organizations that scale (not just teams that ship)
Driven cross-org alignment in ambiguous spaces

Product + Systems Thinking

You think in systems, not features.

You understand how user workflows connect end-to-end
You’ve partnered deeply with Product and Design
You care about customer outcomes, not just technical output

You’ve built or led production LLM/agentic systems

You’ve seen systems fail and improved them
You have opinions about evaluation, reliability, and safety

You can move fast without breaking everything.

You’ve balanced shipping vs infrastructure vs tech debt
You know when to iterate and when to redesign

This is not “AI theatre.”

We already have:

AI Receptionist (live, handling real customer calls)
AI features embedded across the product
250,000+ businesses using the platform

jobs.description:
Most finance executives inherit a system. You will redesign one, then decide where the capital goes.

Trilogy is looking for the executive who can turn a portfolio of businesses into a capital allocation system: continuously ranking where the next dollar should go, backing those decisions with rigorous models, and moving capital toward its highest-return uses. You will own the calls that matter: fund or kill a business line; invest or hold; acquire or walk away; refinance or pay down debt. Every recommendation must connect strategy to cash, liquidity, covenants, risk, and enterprise value.

Just as important, you will architect an AI-native finance function built to scale without decision bottlenecks. This does not mean sprinkling AI tools onto a traditional finance organization. You will redesign reporting, planning, controls, portfolio monitoring, and decision support around what AI and automation can now do. You won't need to personally build every workflow, but you must use AI deeply enough to know its edges: where it accelerates analysis, where it fails, and where expert judgment must take over. The result should be a smaller, more senior, higher-leverage finance organization rather than a growing pyramid of people and processes.

You will operate directly with Trilogy's CEO, board, lenders, and capital partners, with personal accountability for the financial truth behind major decisions. This is an $800K W-2 salaried role for someone who has already earned credibility at serious financial scale and now wants the mandate to compound enterprise value across an entire portfolio. If you want your impact measured by the quality of your capital decisions and the financial system you leave behind, apply.

What You Will Be Doing

Allocating capital across the portfolio: Run capital and portfolio reviews, rank competing uses of capital on risk-adjusted return, and make clear fund, hold, restructure, exit, debt-paydown, or acquisition recommendations.
Architecting an AI-native finance system: Redesign planning, reporting, consolidation, controls, portfolio monitoring, and financial workflows around AI, automation, and scalable systems rather than additional headcount.
Driving investments and transactions: Build and defend the financial case for strategic investments, M&A, financing, and refinancing, including integrated models, downside scenarios, capital structure, covenant implications, and execution plans.
Owning board and capital-partner communication: Give the CEO, board, lenders, and capital partners fast, quantified, defensible truth, with recommendations that make the decision and trade-offs explicit.
Building a high-leverage finance leadership team: Set the bar for a small group of exceptional finance leaders while creating systems that allow new ventures and greater complexity to be absorbed without linear organizational growth.

What You Won’t Be Doing

Running finance as a reporting factory. Closing the books and producing audit workpapers are the Controller's responsibilities. Your job is to turn financial information into better capital decisions.
Building a large finance organization to handle complexity. Scale should come from better systems, AI leverage, automation, and exceptional people, not layers of management.
Adding AI as a superficial productivity tool. You will architect workflows around its real capabilities and limitations, which requires substantial firsthand use.
Producing strategy decks without financial consequences. Major recommendations must carry the integrated model, downside case, capital implications, and execution guardrails behind them.
Managing the board through narrative. The numbers, assumptions, risks, and recommended action should be clear enough to withstand scrutiny.

Executive Vice President And Chief Financial Officer Key Responsibilities

Build a durable, AI-native finance function that compounds enterprise value across Trilogy's portfolio by allocating capital to its highest-return uses and creating financial systems and controls that scale without decision bottlenecks.

Basic Requirements

Experience as the most senior finance decision-maker, or their direct deputy, for a business or portfolio with $100M+ in annual revenue across multiple legal entities.
Personal ownership of major capital-allocation decisions, including the ability to explain what was funded, reduced, or rejected; the dollars involved; the trade-offs; and your recommendation.
Decision ownership on at least one $25M+ closed M&A, financing, or refinancing transaction, with direct responsibility for negotiation, financing selection, board recommendation, or post-close integration.
Direct experience presenting to and taking live questions from a board of directors.
Ownership of an external audit relationship under US GAAP or IFRS, directly or through a Controller reporting to you.
Hands-on experience with a true enterprise ERP such as SAP, NetSuite, Oracle, Workday, or equivalent.
Recent experience re-architecting a finance workflow around AI, with enough regular personal AI use to understand where the technology is reliable, where it is not, and how those boundaries should shape finance-system design.
Ability to operate integrated 3-statement models and defend assumptions, downside scenarios, covenant math, capital structure, and recommendations under live questioning.
Strong written and verbal English, with experience communicating directly with CEOs, boards, lenders, or capital partners.
Located within the UTC−8 to UTC+3 time-zone range.

Nice-to-have Requirements

CPA, ACA, ACCA, CIMA, CFA, MBA, or comparable finance credential.
Earlier career experience in private equity, investment banking, M&A, corporate finance, or another environment requiring rigorous modeling and high-stakes capital decisions.
Experience rebuilding a finance function rather than simply inheriting and operating one.
Experience across a portfolio, multi-entity, or PE-backed operating environment.

About Trilogy

Hundreds of software businesses run on the Trilogy Business Platform. For three decades, Trilogy has been known for 3 things: Relentlessly seeking top talent, innovating new technology, and incubating new businesses.

Our technological innovation is spearheaded by a passion for simple customer-facing designs. Our incubation of new businesses ranges from entirely new moon-shot ideas to rearchitecting existing projects for today's modern cloud-based stack.

Trilogy is a place where you can be surrounded with great people, be proud of doing great work, and grow your career in leaps and bounds.

There is so much to cover for this exciting role, and space here is limited. Hit the Apply button if you found this interesting and want to learn more. We look forward to meeting you!

Working with us

The position is immediately available and requires entering into an independent contractor agreement with Crossover as a Contractor of Record. The compensation level for this role is $400 USD/hour, which equates to $800,000 USD/year assuming 40 hours per week and 50 weeks per year. The payment period is weekly. Most finance executives inherit a system. You will redesign one, then decide where the capital goes.

Trilogy is looking for the executive who can turn a portfolio of businesses into a capital allocation system: continuously ranking where the next dollar should go, backing those decisions with rigorous models, and moving capital toward its highest-return uses. You will own the calls that matter: fund or kill a business line; invest or hold; acquire or walk away; refinance or pay down debt. Every recommendation must connect strategy to cash, liquidity, covenants, risk, and enterprise value.

Just as important, you will architect an AI-native finance function built to scale without decision bottlenecks. This does not mean sprinkling AI tools onto a traditional finance organization. You will redesign reporting, planning, controls, portfolio monitoring, and decision support around what AI and automation can now do. You won't need to personally build every workflow, but you must use AI deeply enough to know its edges: where it accelerates analysis, where it fails, and where expert judgment must take over. The result should be a smaller, more senior, higher-leverage finance organization rather than a growing pyramid of people and processes.

You will operate directly with Trilogy's CEO, board, lenders, and capital partners, with personal accountability for the financial truth behind major decisions. This is an $800K W-2 salaried role for someone who has already earned credibility at serious financial scale and now wants the mandate to compound enterprise value across an entire portfolio. If you want your impact measured by the quality of your capital decisions and the financial system you leave behind, apply.

What You Will Be Doing

Allocating capital across the portfolio: Run capital and portfolio reviews, rank competing uses of capital on risk-adjusted return, and make clear fund, hold, restructure, exit, debt-paydown, or acquisition recommendations.
Architecting an AI-native finance system: Redesign planning, reporting, consolidation, controls, portfolio monitoring, and financial workflows around AI, automation, and scalable systems rather than additional headcount.
Driving investments and transactions: Build and defend the financial case for strategic investments, M&A, financing, and refinancing, including integrated models, downside scenarios, capital structure, covenant implications, and execution plans.
Owning board and capital-partner communication: Give the CEO, board, lenders, and capital partners fast, quantified, defensible truth, with recommendations that make the decision and trade-offs explicit.
Building a high-leverage finance leadership team: Set the bar for a small group of exceptional finance leaders while creating systems that allow new ventures and greater complexity to be absorbed without linear organizational growth.

What You Won’t Be Doing

Running finance as a reporting factory. Closing the books and producing audit workpapers are the Controller's responsibilities. Your job is to turn financial information into better capital decisions.
Building a large finance organization to handle complexity. Scale should come from better systems, AI leverage, automation, and exceptional people, not layers of management.
Adding AI as a superficial productivity tool. You will architect workflows around its real capabilities and limitations, which requires substantial firsthand use.
Producing strategy decks without financial consequences. Major recommendations must carry the integrated model, downside case, capital implications, and execution guardrails behind them.
Managing the board through narrative. The numbers, assumptions, risks, and recommended action should be clear enough to withstand scrutiny.

Executive Vice President And Chief Financial Officer Key Responsibilities

Most finance executives inherit a system. You will redesign one, then decide where the capital goes.

Trilogy is looking for the executive who can turn a portfolio of businesses into a capital allocation system: continuously ranking where the next dollar should go, backing those decisions with rigorous models, and moving capital toward its highest-return uses. You will own the calls that matter: fund or kill a business line; invest or hold; acquire or walk away; refinance or pay down debt. Every recommendation must connect strategy to cash, liquidity, covenants, risk, and enterprise value.

Just as important, you will architect an AI-native finance function built to scale without decision bottlenecks. This does not mean sprinkling AI tools onto a traditional finance organization. You will redesign reporting, planning, controls, portfolio monitoring, and decision support around what AI and automation can now do. You won't need to personally build every workflow, but you must use AI deeply enough to know its edges: where it accelerates analysis, where it fails, and where expert judgment must take over. The result should be a smaller, more senior, higher-leverage finance organization rather than a growing pyramid of people and processes.

You will operate directly with Trilogy's CEO, board, lenders, and capital partners, with personal accountability for the financial truth behind major decisions. This is an $800K W-2 salaried role for someone who has already earned credibility at serious financial scale and now wants the mandate to compound enterprise value across an entire portfolio. If you want your impact measured by the quality of your capital decisions and the financial system you leave behind, apply.

What You Will Be Doing

Allocating capital across the portfolio: Run capital and portfolio reviews, rank competing uses of capital on risk-adjusted return, and make clear fund, hold, restructure, exit, debt-paydown, or acquisition recommendations.
Architecting an AI-native finance system: Redesign planning, reporting, consolidation, controls, portfolio monitoring, and financial workflows around AI, automation, and scalable systems rather than additional headcount.
Driving investments and transactions: Build and defend the financial case for strategic investments, M&A, financing, and refinancing, including integrated models, downside scenarios, capital structure, covenant implications, and execution plans.
Owning board and capital-partner communication: Give the CEO, board, lenders, and capital partners fast, quantified, defensible truth, with recommendations that make the decision and trade-offs explicit.
Building a high-leverage finance leadership team: Set the bar for a small group of exceptional finance leaders while creating systems that allow new ventures and greater complexity to be absorbed without linear organizational growth.

What You Won’t Be Doing

Running finance as a reporting factory. Closing the books and producing audit workpapers are the Controller's responsibilities. Your job is to turn financial information into better capital decisions.

new_jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Strategic Business Executive
new_jobs.description:
Come... Enjoy... Work
in a fast paced, dynamic environment. Located on the Tsuut’ina First Nation, Grey Eagle Resort & Casino is Calgary’s number one entertainment facility. We are looking for talented, energetic and motivated individuals to join our diverse workforce! We offer competitive salaries, benefits and opportunities to grow your career.

Position Overview

The Chief Financial Officer (CFO) is a key executive leader responsible for the financial stewardship, strategic planning, governance support, and long-term sustainability of Grey Eagle Resort & Casino (GERC).

Reporting directly to the Board of Directors, the CFO serves as the principal financial advisor to the Board and Executive Leadership Team, providing leadership across financial operations, capital investment planning, enterprise risk management, business growth initiatives, and stakeholder relations.

The CFO plays a critical role in supporting the Board's vision for sustainable economic growth while protecting and enhancing the assets of Grey Eagle Resort & Casino for future generations of the Tsuut'ina Nation.

The role oversees all financial functions and provides executive leadership for major capital projects, resort renovations, business development initiatives, financing strategies, and governance matters affecting the organization.

As one of the most senior leaders within GERC, the CFO must balance strategic thinking, operational understanding, financial discipline, and relationship-building with a diverse group of stakeholders including the Board of Directors, Tsuut'ina Nation leadership, regulators, financial institutions, development partners, and operational leaders.

Education And Experience

CPA designation.
Bachelor's Degree in Accounting, Finance, Commerce, or related discipline.
Minimum 10 years progressive financial leadership experience.
Minimum 5 years in a senior executive role.
Experience in hospitality, gaming, resort, entertainment, tourism, real estate development, or similarly complex operations.
Experience reporting directly to a Board of Directors.
Experience leading major capital projects exceeding $10M.
Demonstrated success managing banking and financing relationships.

Preferred

MBA or Master's Degree.
Experience working with Indigenous-owned organizations, governments, or economic development entities.
Experience in a regulated gaming environment.
Experience supporting Board committees and governance functions.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Strategic Leadership & Board Support

Serve as the primary financial advisor to the Board of Directors.
Provide recommendations on strategic initiatives, capital investments, financing structures, business growth opportunities, and organizational performance.
Prepare and present comprehensive financial and operational reports to the Board.
Support the Board in strategic planning and long-term sustainability initiatives.
Participate in governance discussions and provide financial guidance regarding organizational priorities.
Assist the Board in evaluating significant business opportunities, acquisitions, partnerships, and development projects.

________________________________________

Financial Leadership & Stewardship

Lead all aspects of financial management and reporting.
Develop and execute financial strategies aligned with organizational goals.
Oversee:
Budgeting, Forecasting, Financial Reporting
Treasury Management, Cash Flow Management
Internal Controls
Tax Compliance
Audit Functions
Capital Planning
Ensure financial integrity and accountability throughout the organization.
Establish and monitor key performance indicators and financial metrics.

________________________________________

Capital Projects, Renovation & Development Oversight

The CFO will provide executive leadership for capital investment planning and project governance across the resort.

Responsibilities Include

Develop long-term capital investment strategies.
Oversee financial planning and governance for renovation and expansion projects.
Lead financial evaluation and business case development for all major capital expenditures.
Monitor project budgets, timelines, risks, and return on investment.
Ensure appropriate project controls and reporting mechanisms are in place.

________________________________________

Master Site Development Planning

Participate in long-term master planning for Grey Eagle Resort & Casino lands and facilities.
Evaluate future development opportunities through financial modeling and strategic analysis.
Support land use planning, phased development initiatives, and infrastructure investment decisions.
Provide financial leadership related to future resort expansion opportunities.
Collaborate with Nation leadership, developers, consultants, and external advisors regarding future growth initiatives.

________________________________________

Banking, Financing & Capital Structure Management

Lead relationships with financial institutions and lending partners.
Develop financing strategies to support operational and capital requirements.
Negotiate banking agreements, credit facilities, and financing arrangements.
Manage cash reserves and liquidity planning.
Advise the Board regarding capital structure optimization and debt management strategies.

________________________________________

Hotel Asset Management & Resort Performance

Provide strategic oversight regarding the financial performance of hotel and resort assets.
Evaluate asset performance and investment priorities.
Support lifecycle planning for hotel, gaming, entertainment, and food & beverage facilities.
Monitor asset utilization and return on investment.
Develop recommendations regarding reinvestment and asset enhancement opportunities.

________________________________________

Casino Reinvestment Strategy

Develop and maintain a long-term casino reinvestment strategy.
Assess gaming floor performance and capital replacement needs.
Support strategic decisions regarding gaming technology and facility improvements.
Ensure reinvestment planning aligns with market conditions and guest expectations.
Evaluate opportunities to enhance competitiveness and profitability.

________________________________________

iGaming Strategy, Financial Oversight & Business Development

Provide executive financial leadership for the establishment, launch, growth, and ongoing financial performance of GERC's iGaming business unit.
Lead financial modelling, budgeting, forecasting, capital planning, and business-case evaluation related to iGaming operations and strategic initiatives.
Establish and oversee appropriate financial reporting, revenue assurance, reconciliation, treasury, payment processing, settlement, and internal control frameworks for iGaming activities.
Develop and monitor key iGaming performance indicators, including Gross Gaming Revenue (GGR), Net Gaming Revenue (NGR), gaming margins, customer acquisition costs, promotional and bonus costs, player value, deposits and withdrawals, chargebacks, operating costs, and profitability.
Work collaboratively with iGaming leadership, Compliance, Legal, Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Marketing, and Operations to ensure appropriate financial governance and risk management.
Ensure financial processes, controls, reporting, and recordkeeping support applicable regulatory requirements and GERC's obligations to Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis (AGLC) and the Alberta iGaming Corporation (AiGC).
Provide financial oversight of banking arrangements, payment service providers, gaming technology providers, platform vendors, and other significant iGaming commercial relationships.
Evaluate future iGaming products, partnerships, technology investments, and business expansion opportunities from a financial and strategic perspective.

________________________________________

Procurement Governance

Establish financial oversight and governance for procurement activities.
Ensure transparency, accountability, and value-for-money principles.
Develop policies and controls supporting major purchasing initiatives.
Participate in evaluation and approval processes for significant contracts and vendor relationships.
Ensure procurement activities align with Board-approved financial policies.

________________________________________

Indigenous Relations & Partnership Development

Build and maintain respectful relationships with Tsuut'ina Nation leadership and stakeholders.
Support initiatives that align with the Nation's economic development goals.
Identify opportunities for strategic partnerships that advance organizational objectives.
Participate in partnership discussions with Indigenous and non-Indigenous organizations.
Ensure financial strategies reflect the values and long-term interests of ownership.

________________________________________

Stakeholder Management

The CFO Will Maintain Productive Relationships With

Internal Stakeholders

Board of Directors
Executive Leadership Team
Department Leaders
Team Members

External Stakeholders

Tsuut'ina Nation Leadership
Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis (AGLC)
Alberta iGaming Corporation (AiGC)
Auditors
Financial Institutions
Legal Counsel
Development Partners
Government Agencies
Industry Associations
Consultants and Contractors

________________________________________

Risk Management & Governance

Lead enterprise risk management activities.
Ensure effective internal controls and compliance programs.
Support Board governance and Finance & Audit Committee activities.
Oversee annual external audits.
Ensure compliance with all applicable laws, regulations, and accounting standards.
Develop financial risk mitigation strategies.

________________________________________

BOARD FINANCE & AUDIT COMMITTEE SUPPORT

The CFO serves as management's primary liaison to the Finance and Audit Committee and is responsible for:

Preparing committee materials and recommendations.
Presenting financial results and forecasts.
Supporting audit processes.
Monitoring risk management activities.
Reporting on compliance and internal controls.
Supporting governance best practices.

About Dalhousie University

Dalhousie University is Atlantic Canada’s leading research-intensive university and a driver of the region’s intellectual, social and economic development. Our 6,000 faculty and staff foster a vibrant, purpose-driven community, that celebrated 200 years of academic excellence in 2018.

Job Summary

Dalhousie University, under the leadership of the Vice-President Research & Innovation, administers over $270M annually in research funding. Reporting to the Vice-President Research & Innovation, the Director, Research Facilities and Infrastructure Strategy leads the planning, governance, and sustainability of the University’s research infrastructure portfolio. The Director provides strategic leadership for the University’s research infrastructure, including shared facilities, major equipment platforms, digital research capacity, research computing infrastructure, and associated services.

Key Responsibilities

Lead the development and implementation of Dalhousie’s institutional strategy for research facilities, infrastructure, research computing, and shared research resources, ensuring alignment with university research priorities.

Provide governance and strategic oversight for shared research facilities and programs, including establishing service models, access frameworks, performance expectations, and sustainability plans.

Coordinate cross-faculty and cross-unit planning with stakeholders including Faculties, IT Services, Facilities Management, Research Services, Finance, and external partners to advance infrastructure priorities.
Provide leadership for major university-wide research infrastructure initiatives, stakeholder engagement, and external partnerships that enhance Dalhousie’s research capacity and competitiveness.

Master’s degree with a minimum of seven years’ experience in research administration or related environment (or an equivalent combination of training and experience).
Demonstrated experience providing strategic direction and governance for shared research facilities, core facilities, major research platforms, or institutional research infrastructure programs.
Experience coordinating major research infrastructure funding initiatives, including proposal development, institutional positioning, and compliance reporting for programs such as CFI .
Demonstrated ability to lead complex, multi-stakeholder and cross-faculty initiatives requiring institutional coordination and strategic planning.
Strong analytical, financial oversight, problem-solving, communication, negotiation, and stakeholder engagement skills.
Experience advising senior leadership and developing institutional strategies, governance frameworks, and operational models that support research excellence and infrastructure sustainability.

Experience developing or managing research facilities, infrastructure programs, or capital projects in environments with elevated security, compliance, or regulatory requirements.
